text.p: (Compiled from ABC ARCHIVES, ABC RADIO NATIONAL, "On This Day" published by REED INTERNATIONAL BOOKS LIMITED, "The Chronicle Of The 20th Century" published by PENGUIN BOOKS and "Rock And Pop (Day By Day)" published by BLANDFORD BOOKS.)
BIRTHDAYS
British artist Sir STANLEY SPENCER, who was famous for his biblical scenes, was born in 1891.
American singer LENA HORNE was born in 1917. Her career including several acting roles in movies such as "Cabin In The Sky" and "Stormy Weather".
American actress SUSAN HAYWARD was born in 1918. She won an Oscar for "I Want To Live".
American and world heavyweight boxing champion MIKE TYSON was born in 1966. He will be celebrating his birthday as a free man after being released in early 1995 after sevring a prison term for rape.
EVENTS
1859 : In one of the world's most daring feats a

Frenchman crossed the Niagara Falls on a tightrope. CHARLES BLONDIN took five minutes to walk across the wire strung more than 50 metres above the ground. The 35-year-old acrobat and internationally known tightrope walker stunned the watching crowd. He was on a tour of the United States.
1894 : Tower Bridge in London was officially opened.
1921 : The Chinese Communist party was formed. The first
meeting was held at a girls' school in Shanghai and among those who attended was library assistant and primary school teacher. MAO TSE-TUNG, who became the party's leader. The aim of

the party at its earliest meeting was "the overthrow of the capitalist class". The growth of communism in China closely followed the Russian experience, the revolution and the growth of communism in that country and the rise of a student movement.
1933 : The state of Victoria bought Captain COOK's

cottage in Yorkshire for 800 pounds. The money was a gift from Mr R. GRIMWADE. The two-storey brick and stone cottage was dismantled and packed into 300 cases to be shipped to Australia. The plan caused outrage in Britain and local newspapers called on Victoria to give the cottage back. JAMES COOK grew up in the cottage, which was built in 1755. The cottage was reassembled
and erected in Melbourne's Fitzroy Gardens. The exercise took 18 months from purchase to its opening in Australia. The cottage was opened in October 1934.
1934 : ADOLF HITLER eliminated his political opponents in
the Night of the Long Knives.
1936 : MARGARET MITCHELL's romantic novel "Gone With The
Wind" was published.
1938 : The cartoon character 'SUPERMAN' made his first
appearance. The super hero from the planet Krypton made his debut on the pages of Action Comics. His superhuman powers included 'leaping tall buildings', 'running faster than a

speeding train' and 'possessing the strength of 200 men'. He hid his true identity and crime fighting tendencies by disguising himself as mild-mannered reporter CLARK KENT of the 'Metropolis Daily Globe'. The character has changed little since this first appearance. When trouble arose he would quickly materialise in a 'blue catsuit and red cape, with a big S on his chest'. SUPERMAN print character has since been transformed into a television and movie star, several times.
1960 : The classic ALFRED HITCHCOCK film 'Psycho' opened
to screaming theatre goers. The chilling horror story recalled a killing frenzy by NORMAN BATES. The film was based on a true story of a man who kept his dead mother in the basement.
1971 : Three Russian astronauts were found dead in their
spaceship after a record-breaking 24 days in space. They died after their craft experienced oxygen failure in the final stage of the journey.
1974 : Russian ballet dancer MIKHAIL BARYSHNIKOV defected
to the West while on tour in Canada with the Bolshoi Ballet.
1981 : The Queen was the target of a "pretend"

assassination attempt. A youth stepped from the crowds at the Trooping of the Colours in London and fired a pistol at ELIZABETH II. Police acted quickly and immediately arrested the youth. It was the discovered he had been firing blanks.
